newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY'S NEW POLICE CHIEF PRESSED TO GET RESULTS.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY'S NEW POLICE CHIEF PRESSED TO GET RESULTS.

text.p: Hungary's new police chief, began his first day on Monday under strong public pressure to get results following a series of unsolved bombings and shootings in Budapest.

Laszlo Forgacs, 47, replaces Sandor Pinter, sacked two weeks ago along with three other police chiefs by Minister of Interior Gabor Kuncze, for failing to make headway in what observers believe is a gang war in the capital.
Since September, Budapest citizens have been rattled by twelve bombings and five armed attacks against people who are believed to have become involved in a war of organised gangs.
One man was killed in the shootings and two more severely injured. The explosions have not injured anyone but have caused serious damage.

Kuncze said he expected Forgacs to improve on Pinter's performance and has commanded him to introduce a complete overhaul of the national police, making it leaner, more cost-effective and giving back some authority to regional police headquarters.
Kuncze said he trusted Forgacs "to be able to produce changes in a very short time".
However, on Sunday evening Forgacs cautioned the population against expecting immediate results regarding the capital's current crime wave.
"It's going to be a long hard job," he told Hungarian television on Sunday night.
Forgacs began his career 24 years ago as a detective in Hungary's poorest county Borsod and worked his way up to county police chief in 1992.

Hungary's press has painted Forgacs as intolerant of any whiff of corruption. Under his command, the Borsod force has 10 percent better record for solving crimes than the national average, reports say.
Forgacs's appointment has broken a recent tradition of nominating a law graduate as national police chief.
"I'm just a policeman and I'll stay a policeman," he said.
